# Scholar Evaluation

Curated by Skill Harbor: a structured evaluation workflow for academic and scientific work, from the affaan-m/ECC community contributions. Handles empirical and theoretical papers, technical reports, systematic or narrative literature reviews, research proposals, thesis chapters, and conference abstracts. Scores nine dimensions from 1 to 5: problem and research question, literature and context, methodology, data and evidence, analysis, results and interpretation, limitations and threats to validity, writing and structure, and citations. Includes a defined review process (read abstract, introduction, figures, and conclusion first for the claimed contribution; check the strongest claims against cited sources; separate critical blockers from revision suggestions) and a ready output template with dimension scores, evidence, and revision priority. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: a rubric, not peer review; the score is a summary, never a substitute for concrete feedback. Do not penalize a paper for omitting a dimension outside its scope, and do not treat venue or author reputation as proof of quality. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
